test_title: PYST 29: SSC GD Constable 2025 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 18 Feb, 2025 - Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: Raj has ₹1218 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Varun and Ashish and asked them to invest it at 10% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Varun and Ashish got same amount after 13 and 14 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Raj give to Ashish?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If amounts are equal after T₁ and T₂ years, then P₁ / P₂ = (1 + R/100)T² − T¹

Here, Ratio of Varun's share to Ashish's share (V/A) = (1 + 10/100)¹⁴ − ¹³ = 11/10

Total ratio parts = 11 + 10 = 21 parts

21 parts = 1218 ⇒ 1 part = 1218 ÷ 21 = 58

Ashish's share (10 parts) = 10 × 58 = 580

**∴ The correct answer is ₹580.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Amount = ₹1218

Rate (R) = 10% compounded annually

Time for Varun = 13 years

Time for Ashish = 14 years

**Formula Used:**

Compound Interest Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)T
